baby-toddler-fruit-vegetables-and-meat.title: Baby Toddler fruit, vegetables, and meat

content.title: About
content.content: This blend of fruit, vegetables and meat is designed for babies and toddlers from 6 months to 3 years. It contains carefully selected soft fruits, cooked vegetables and tender meat, prepared without added salt, sugar or artificial flavours. The product provides a variety of tastes and essential nutrients needed for healthy growth and development.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fruits and vegetables are steam‑cooked to retain most of their vitamins and minerals.
The meat component is usually chicken or turkey, lean and easy to digest for a young stomach.
The blend is free from gluten and dairy, making it suitable for children with intolerances.
Each serving is sized for one meal and contains roughly 70–90 kcal, facilitating calorie control.
The product meets strict infant‑food safety standards in the EU and the US.

items.title: Rich in vitamins A and C
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision and immunity, while vitamin C aids iron absorption and protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of iron and zinc
items.content: Meat provides highly bioavailable iron and zinc, essential for blood formation and immune function.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the fruit and vegetables promotes healthy bowel movements and helps develop a balanced gut microbiome.

items.title: Low in sodium
items.content: No added salt helps establish a healthy taste preference early in life.

items.title: Easily digestible protein
items.content: Lean meat supplies the amino acids needed for muscle and organ growth.

items.title: Allergy to food components
items.content: Some children may be allergic to the fruit, vegetable or meat. Introduce a small amount first and monitor for reactions.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Although the product is a puree, large lumps can form if not mixed properly. Always check consistency before serving.

items.title: Natural fruit sugars
items.content: Fruits contain natural fructose; families with a history of diabetes should consult a pediatrician.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the product as a smooth puree or a soft mash. You may thin it with breast milk, formula, or water to reach the desired consistency. For children over 12 months, small soft pieces of cooked vegetable or meat can be mixed in.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened package in a cool, dry place. Once opened, store in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C and use within 48 hours. Do not freeze. Discard if you notice off‑odors, discoloration or mold.

chicken-or-turkey-potatoes-and-vegetable.title: Chicken or turkey with potatoes and vegetables without carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens, no sauce

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of roasted or boiled chicken or turkey, potatoes and a selection of vegetables, excluding carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens. It is prepared without any sauces, making it light and nutritious.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey provide complete protein containing all essential amino acids.
Potatoes are one of the world’s most consumed root vegetables and are rich in vitamin C and potassium.
Excluding carrots and broccoli reduces beta‑carotene content while retaining other vitamins and minerals from the remaining vegetables.
A sauce‑free preparation is suitable for people monitoring salt and sugar intake.
When stored properly, the ingredients stay fresh for 3‑4 days in the refrigerator.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Poultry meat supplies high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Potassium and magnesium
items.content: Potatoes and vegetables provide potassium and magnesium, supporting heart and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin B6
items.content: Chicken and turkey are high in vitamin B6, which is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: The absence of sauces and sweet ingredients makes the dish suitable for blood‑glucose control.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetables and potatoes add dietary fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to proteins found in chicken or turkey.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the meat was pre‑salted, sodium levels can be high; use minimal added salt.

items.title: Potential bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked poultry may harbor pathogens; ensure internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

items.title: Foodborne illness from improperly stored vegetables
items.content: Vegetables left at room temperature for more than 2 hours can become a source of bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course, or pair it with whole‑grain sides such as quinoa or brown rice. Vegetables can be served in large chunks or mashed, and the meat sliced into strips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then place it in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat to at least 75 °C before serving.

potato-boiled-from-fresh-peel-eaten-ns-a.title: Boiled Potato, fresh, peel eaten, NS for fat

content.title: About
content.content: Boiled potato is fresh potato tubers cooked in salted water until tender. The skin is left on and eaten, adding extra fiber and micronutrients to the dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato is one of the most widely consumed vegetables worldwide.
Boiling preserves most of the vitamin C if the water is not discarded.
The skin of boiled potatoes contains more potassium and iron than the flesh.
Different cultures serve boiled potatoes with a variety of sauces and seasonings.
There is a tradition of "potato evenings" where the dish is served in salads or as a side.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Both the skin and flesh provide dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are a good source of potassium, which helps maintain heart and muscle function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Boiled potatoes contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain vitamins B6 and B9, important for metabolism and blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: The skin holds antioxidant compounds such as phenolics that combat free radicals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Adding salt to the cooking water can increase sodium levels, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Boiled potatoes have a high glycemic index and can raise blood sugar quickly.

items.title: Solanine risk
items.content: If potatoes are damaged or sprouted, the skin may contain solanine, a toxic compound that should be avoided.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled potatoes can be eaten plain, sliced into salads, mashed, or used in casseroles. Keeping the skin on preserves additional nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store boiled potatoes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Over time they may become dry and lose flavor.

shrimp-and-noodles-with-cheese-sauce.title: Shrimp and noodles with cheese sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp and noodles with cheese sauce is a dish that combines seafood, pasta and a creamy cheese‑based sauce. The shrimp cook quickly, while the noodles (usually egg noodles or spaghetti) soak up the flavorful sauce, creating a hearty and aromatic meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The shrimp‑and‑cheese combination is popular in Asian‑European fusion cuisine, where creamy sauces are used to mellow the taste of seafood.
Shrimp are high‑protein and low‑calorie, making the dish suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.
The cheese sauce can be made from various cheeses: cheddar, parmesan, mozzarella or cream cheese, each giving a distinct flavor profile.
Traditionally the noodles are cooked al dente to retain texture and avoid turning mushy in the sauce.
Quick sauté of shrimp until pink preserves their tenderness and prevents overcooking.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Shrimp provide complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many meat dishes, shrimp contain little saturated fat, supporting heart‑healthy eating.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: Shrimp are a good source of selenium, zinc and iodine, which support immune function and thyroid health.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is important for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Balanced carbohydrates
items.content: The noodles supply energy, and the protein‑carb pairing helps moderate blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people monitoring their cholesterol should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium in the sauce
items.content: Cheese sauces are often salty; those with hypertension should reduce added salt or use low‑sodium cheese.

items.title: Additives in prepared sauces
items.content: Store‑bought sauces may contain preservatives and flavor enhancers; homemade sauce is preferable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, garnished with fresh herbs such as parsley or dill and a wedge of lemon. Add vegetables like broccoli, peas or bell pepper for extra volume and nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. When reheating, stir in a splash of milk or cream to restore the sauce’s creamy texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Tuna salad with light mayonnaise is a ready‑to‑eat dish where cooked or canned tuna is mixed with a reduced‑fat mayonnaise, fresh vegetables, and sometimes herbs or spices. Light mayonnaise contains fewer calories and less fat than traditional versions, making the salad more diet‑friendly.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tuna is one of the richest sources of omega‑3 fatty acids, which are beneficial for heart health.
Light mayonnaise is often made with yogurt or plant‑based oils, lowering saturated fat content.
Athletes and weight‑watchers frequently include tuna salad in their meal plans.
Tuna packed in its own juice retains more nutrients compared to tuna canned in oil.
In Japan a similar dish is called “tuna‑salad” and is commonly used as a filling for sushi rolls.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids support cardiovascular health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Tuna provides a complete amino acid profile, aiding muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Using light mayonnaise cuts the overall calorie count, making the dish suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tuna supplies B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The salad contains selenium, phosphorus, and potassium, supporting immune function and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: People allergic to seafood should avoid tuna salad.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Tuna can contain trace amounts of mercury; pregnant women and children should limit intake.

items.title: Sodium in canned tuna
items.content: Canned tuna is often high in salt, which may be a concern for those with hypertension.

items.title: Quality of mayonnaise
items.content: Some light mayonnaises contain additives; choose versions without artificial preservatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a standalone dish, in sandwiches, wraps, or as a side to vegetable plates. Add cucumber, tomato, fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or a dash of mustard to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, keep the mayonnaise separate from the tuna to prevent the vegetables from becoming soggy.

content.title: About
content.content: Plain whole‑milk yogurt is made by fermenting whole cow’s milk with live cultures of Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus. It has a creamy texture, mild milky flavor, and contains about 3.5 % fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yogurt is one of the oldest fermented dairy foods, with evidence of production over 5,000 years ago in Central Asia.
Traditional preparation involves heating milk to 85 °C, cooling to 45 °C, then adding a starter culture.
Live cultures in yogurt can help improve gut microbiota balance.
Plain yogurt is often used as a base for sauces, marinades, and desserts in many cuisines.
Whole‑milk yogurt retains more fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) than low‑fat versions.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Live bacteria support a healthy gut microbiome, which may aid digestion and immune function.

items.title: Calcium and Vitamin D
items.content: Whole milk provides calcium and vitamin D essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Yogurt supplies high‑quality milk protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Fatty Acids
items.content: The fat in whole milk includes conjugated linoleic acid (CLA), studied for potential anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after consuming yogurt.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey requires complete avoidance of the product.

items.title: Higher fat content
items.content: Whole‑milk yogurt is higher in calories and saturated fat; moderation is key for weight management.

items.title: Added sugars in some brands
items.content: While plain yogurt is typically unsweetened, some manufacturers add sugar; check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy yogurt as a snack, blend into smoothies, use as a base for dressings, sauces, desserts, or top with fruit, honey, and nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store yogurt in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
